full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V(K), if x_K(W)⊆W, y_K(W)⊆W and h_K(W)⊆W, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is irreducible for the induced L(K)-action, with no exception for λ=0 or p=2 and no algebraic-closure assumption on K.

parameters.type: complex vector space with a representation of sl₂(ℂ)
complex-linear endomorphism of V representing the raising Chevalley generator

complex-linear endomorphism of V representing the Cartan Chevalley generator

hypotheses.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. The operators x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup having an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_ℤ. M is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

definitions.definition: I={i∈ℕ: i≤λ}, with the natural numbers compared with λ in ℤ.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by ℕ
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ put X_r=(r!)⁻¹x^r; in particular X_0=Id_V. Factorials and inverses here are in ℂ.

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by ℕ
definitions.definition: For r∈ℕ put Y_r=(r!)⁻¹y^r; in particular Y_0=Id_V. Factorials and inverses here are in ℂ.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ), acting on V
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is the ℤ-subalgebra generated by all divided powers X_r and Y_r for r≥0; its action on V is the given representation.

definitions.type: subring of ℚ, also regarded as a subring of ℂ
definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ: a,b∈ℤ, b≠0 and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are inherited from ℚ.
M_R is the R-span of M inside V: its elements are finite sums ∑ r_t m_t with r_t∈R and m_t∈M. The natural multiplication map R⊗_ℤ M→V has this image; its injectivity is to be proved.

binders.type: finite family of elements of R
finite family of elements of M

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms E_ij of V, i,j∈I
definitions.definition: E_ij is the unique complex-linear endomorphism sending e_j to e_i and all e_k with k≠j to zero, using the complex basis e.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of ℂ indexed by I

definitions.definition: J={c∈ℂ: cv∈M_R}; when 0∈I this is J_0 because e_0=v. Equality with all the other J_i is a conclusion, not part of this definition.
V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second tensor factor.
L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y and [x,y]=h. This is the indicated integral Chevalley construction, not a distinct-eigenvalue convention in characteristic 2.
x_K is induced by x on M: x_K(m⊗c)=xm⊗c for m∈M,c∈K.
